solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Company employee providing discipline

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand or deckhand

explanation.surface: A staff member at a business is the one who keeps everyone in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict control over others is described idiomatically as a firm hand.

clue.text: Where office work is seen to be undealt with

definitions.text: Where office work is seen to be undealt with

parts.words: Where office work is seen to be undealt with
parts.note: the tray on a desk holding incoming papers that still await attention

explanation.surface: A look at the pile of tasks nobody has got round to yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk tray for incoming documents holds the pending items still awaiting action.

clue.text: A maxim spoken by many

parts.note: a lesson or principle drawn from a story, repeated by lots of people

explanation.surface: A saying that lots of people repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesson at the end of a fable is a short principle of conduct, a kind of maxim.

clue.text: Taken on and taken off without reason

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: to take someone off is to mimic them, so taken off means aped
the point of something is its purpose or reason

explanation.surface: Someone hired and then mocked for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', which would make 'without reason' read as 'pointlessly'; here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed has been given a post, that is, hired or taken on.

clue.text: China ends Red revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country's communist revolution comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is the porcelain, not the country: Dresden is a German city famous for fine porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a type of fine porcelain, and porcelain ware is called china.

clue.text: Crooked female of nursery rhyme

parts.note: the shepherdess in the rhyme who lost her sheep carries a crook, so she is crooked in a playful sense

explanation.surface: A dishonest woman from a children's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's little shepherdess is traditionally drawn holding a shepherd's crook.

clue.text: Union notices exclude Poles

parts.note: to ban is to bar or exclude
N is the abbreviation for the north pole
S is the abbreviation for the south pole

explanation.surface: A trade union posts a notice banning Polish workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is marriage, not a trade union: the notices of an intended wedding are read in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are the public announcement of a forthcoming marriage, a union.

clue.text: General embargo on place selling cheaper drinks

parts.note: public means general, open to all
an embargo is a bar or ban

explanation.surface: A blanket ban is imposed on a cut-price drinking establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub the public bar is the plainer room where drinks were traditionally cheaper than in the saloon or lounge bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs the basic public bar historically charged less than the more comfortable lounge.

clue.text: Use a lever to give lift

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order, so use signals rearrangement here

explanation.surface: Instructions to prise something up with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' tells you to rework the letters of A LEVER and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word and elevator the American one for the same machine.

clue.text: Rouse the prison to be ready for action

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
up means out of bed and active, ready to go

explanation.surface: A call to provoke the inmates into rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up people is to rouse or provoke them into activity.

clue.text: Entitled to directions before turning blonde

indicators.note: before puts the compass points ahead of the rearranged word

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
N is the abbreviation for north

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to go one way before switching to blonde hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be given a title of nobility, literally entitled.

clue.text: A blow from behind

parts.note: a blow is a gust of air, and this one comes from the rear

explanation.surface: Someone is struck from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from behind a ship or aircraft is a following wind, a blow from behind.

clue.text: April's turned out to be spring-like

indicators.note: turned out signals the letters being rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: April has turned out to be a properly springlike month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring-like' suggests the season, but it means shaped like a coiled spring; the S of April's is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled spring has a spiral shape, so spiral describes something like a spring.

clue.text: Take a tough line to settle motoring cases?

definitions.meaning: to treat someone harshly, kicking them when down
playfully, to stow luggage in the car's boot, British for trunk

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to attack harshly, while suitcases are literally loaded into a car's boot.

clue.text: In favour of moving to get a better job?

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
motion is movement

explanation.surface: Supporting relocation in order to get a better post.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is advancement to a higher-ranking job.

clue.text: In robberies, assume they do things for fun

indicators.note: in places the word for assume inside the word for robberies

parts.note: heists are robberies
to don is to put on or assume, as clothing or a manner

explanation.surface: Thieves who commit robberies just for kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonists are pleasure-seekers, people who pursue enjoyment.

clue.text: Press for a reduction?

definitions.meaning: to iron out creases, read playfully as the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Ironing removes creases, while a decrease is simply a fall or lessening.

clue.text: He has the best time of anyone

definitions.text: He has the best time of anyone

parts.words: He has the best time of anyone
parts.note: not the person enjoying himself most, but the athlete with the fastest time ever

explanation.surface: Someone is having more fun than everybody else.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a world record has the best recorded time of any competitor.

clue.text: One who is against work has a problem

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to labour has some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposer is a person who opposes, standing against something.

clue.text: Tug used in river flood

indicators.note: used in places one word inside another

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to lug is to pull or tug

explanation.surface: A tugboat is put to work in a river in spate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or overwhelming downpour.

clue.text: Gunners go back to the lines for missiles

indicators.note: go back signals the letters of the gunners' abbreviation are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
rows are lines

explanation.surface: Artillerymen retreat to the lines to fetch ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrows are projectiles shot from a bow, hence missiles.

clue.text: Remaining calm

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, even now or yet

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as an adverb for something continuing and an adjective meaning motionless or tranquil.

clue.text: Dad arrested — took fright

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
nicked is British slang for arrested

explanation.surface: Father was taken in by the police and was terrified.
explanation.definitionFit: To have panicked is to have been overcome by sudden fear.

clue.text: Shanty for the rest of the sailors

definitions.text: Shanty for the rest of the sailors

parts.words: Shanty for the rest of the sailors
parts.note: shanty suggests a sea song, but it is a rough hut, and the sailors rest in a room on board

explanation.surface: A sea song sung by the remaining crew members.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is both a simple hut and a sleeping room on a ship.

clue.text: In guinea pigs it may result in loss of teeth

definitions.text: may result in loss of teeth

indicators.note: in places the little word inside the word for guinea pigs

parts.note: cavies are guinea pigs and their South American relatives

explanation.surface: Something in guinea pigs causes their teeth to fall out.
explanation.definitionFit: Holes from tooth decay can lead to teeth being lost.

clue.text: Master of vessel expected

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
due means expected, as in a train due at noon

explanation.surface: The captain of the ship is due to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or subdue it.

clue.text: King Charles's residence?

parts.note: not the monarch's palace but the home of a King Charles spaniel, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Where does the king live?
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of the King Charles spaniel breed would live in a doghouse.

clue.text: Taken ill

parts.note: not fallen sick but taken badly, in the old phrase to take something ill

explanation.definitionFit: To take something ill is to be offended by it, which means feeling aggrieved.
